You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer runtime-linux):
- file: runtime/linux/mm.c:20
- category: duplication
- title: Linux errno constants defined twice across mm.c and syscall.c
- detail: mm.c lines 20-22 define ENOMEM 12, EINVAL 22, ENOSYS 38; syscall.c lines 103-106 define EINVAL 22, ENOTTY 25, ERANGE 34, ENOSYS 38 -- EINVAL and ENOSYS are defined in both files. They cannot use the toolchain's <errno.h> (newlib's ENOSYS is 88, not Linux's 38, which is why local defines exist at all -- vlinux must return LINUX numbers to the glibc app), so the right home is one small vlinux-local header (e.g. runtime/linux/linux_errno.h) included by both, preventing the two copies from drifting when the next syscall needs a new errno.
- claimed safety: Same numeric values, moved to a shared header; preprocessor output for both TUs is unchanged.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

1	#ifndef VLINUX_MM_H
2	#define VLINUX_MM_H
3	
4	#include <stdint.h>

6	/* Set the brk arena's floor (the app's own image end -- loaded_elf.image_end)
7	 * and the mmap arena's ceiling (mem_size minus stack.h's 8 MiB stack
8	 * reservation -- "just below the app stack", the roadmap's guest memory
9	 * map). Must be called once, before any sys_brk/sys_mmap call. */
10	void mm_init(uint64_t app_image_end, uint64_t mem_size);
11	
12	/* The manifest's guest RAM size, for sys_sysinfo's totalram/freeram. */
13	uint64_t mm_total_ram(void);
14	
15	/* brk(2): addr==0 queries the current break; otherwise tries to set it.
16	 * Linux syscall convention: always returns the RESULTING break (old value
17	 * on failure, not -1) -- glibc's brk() wrapper compares it against what it
18	 * asked for. */
19	long sys_brk(unsigned long addr);
20	
21	/* mmap(2): bump-allocates from the top of the mmap arena downward.
22	 * MAP_ANONYMOUS is zeroed (the POSIX guarantee); `addr` is ignored (no
23	 * MAP_FIXED support). MAP_PRIVATE file-backed (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md
24	 * U7, llama.cpp's default GGUF load path): the [offset, offset+length)
25	 * range is eagerly read (htif_pread) into the freshly-allocated arena
26	 * space -- a real, private, independently-owned COPY, which is exactly
27	 * what MAP_PRIVATE promises (writes never propagate back to the file;
28	 * there is simply nowhere for this relay to route them even if it wanted
29	 * to). MAP_SHARED is not supported (-ENOSYS): this relay has no way to
30	 * write a shared mapping's changes back to the host file. Returns a
31	 * negative errno on failure, matching the raw syscall (not the libc
32	 * wrapper's -1 + errno) convention. */
33	long sys_mmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot,
34	             long flags, long fd, long offset);
35	
36	/* munmap(2)/mprotect(2): the bump allocator never reclaims or changes
37	 * protection (there is no MMU here -- every page is already RWX), so both
38	 * are accepted no-ops for ANY address/length, mapped or not -- POSIX
39	 * itself allows this (munmap(2): "it is not an error if the indicated
40	 * range does not contain any mapped pages"), so llama.cpp's partial
41	 * unmap of an unused GGUF tail range is answered correctly without
42	 * needing to track individual mappings. A real munmap would let the
43	 * arena run out sooner than it should; that is a leak, not a crash. */
44	long sys_munmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length);
45	long sys_mprotect(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot);
46	
47	/* mremap(2): always refused (-ENOMEM, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U7) -- the
48	 * bump allocator has no in-place-grow or relocate-and-copy capability, so
49	 * a caller (llama.cpp does not use this for GGUF loading) gets a loud,
50	 * correct failure instead of silent corruption. */
51	long sys_mremap(unsigned long old_addr, unsigned long old_size,
52	                unsigned long new_size, unsigned long flags);

54	#endif /* VLINUX_MM_H */

input.description: Check for existing errno headers and includes of shared runtime headers

input.reason: Verified both sites: mm.c:20-22 (ENOMEM 12, EINVAL 22, ENOSYS 38) and syscall.c:103-106 (EINVAL 22, ENOTTY 25, ERANGE 34, ENOSYS 38) duplicate EINVAL/ENOSYS with identical values, so consolidating into one vlinux-local header yields byte-identical preprocessor output for both TUs. The can't-use-<errno.h> rationale is correct (Makefile uses the newlib riscv64-unknown-elf toolchain, whose ENOSYS is 88, while the glibc app needs Linux's 38). No collision or exposure: repo-wide grep shows these macros exist only in these two .c files, neither TU includes <errno.h> or any header defining E* macros, no *errno* header name exists in andesim or andesim-demo, and TU-private #defines cannot be referenced from the vsim repo. Only build output is vlinux.elf (no header install), so no observable behavior can change; the new header should also be added to the Makefile's HDRS list for rebuild tracking (non-behavioral).
